neural responses are variable and can be flexibly modeled by a sparse Gaussian process that captures variability modulation by external and internal covariates.

variability in neural activity can be modulated as much as the mean rate and that slow latent factors explain away correlations between neurons.

The main takeaway from our work is that

variability is a fundamental property of neural responses, which is modulated by sensory inputs, behavioural states and latent factors, and that this modulation is as strong as that of the mean response.
the neural variability that we observe under naturalistic conditions is not just noise but rather a rich source of information that is shaped by the brain’s computations and dynamics.
